finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the unsanitized query parameter `f` is joined to the root directory. filepath.Join cleans `..` segments but does not confine the result to root, so an attacker can read any file the process can read.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (files.go:12), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18.

trace.note: The /dl route is registered with no auth middleware.
name is taken directly from r.URL.Query().Get("f").
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", which escapes the root; os.ReadFile then reads it.
The file contents are returned to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: There is no prefix check after Join, no filepath.Base, no os.Root or fs.FS confinement, and no allowlist. There is also no authentication or authorization on the route. The sibling handler avatar() uses filepath.Base, which shows the guard was missed here. Example request: GET /dl?f=../../etc/passwd.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query parameter `f` straight into filepath.Join(root, name) and os.ReadFile, with no prefix check or Base, and files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth, so `../../etc/passwd` is read and returned at files.go:18.
